column2: Retain Abijah's accession in Jeroboam's eighteenth year and rule over Judah. The synchronism is not adjusted to resolve an external chronology.
Retain three years, Maacah daughter of Ouriel from Gabaon and warfare with Jeroboam. Do not change the mother to Michaiah, the place to Gibeah or the father to Absalom to harmonize other notices.
Retain Abijah's 400,000 and Jeroboam's 800,000, with the repeated strength/warrior descriptions. No reduced figures or reconstructed counting units are substituted.
Retain Mount Somoron in Ephraim's hill country and the address to Jeroboam and all Israel. The selected mountain name is not replaced by a different traditional name.
Retain the rhetorical knowledge question, enduring Davidic kingship and covenant of salt. The salt metaphor remains unexpanded rather than being replaced with an explanatory permanence gloss.
Retain Jeroboam son of Nabat, service to Solomon son of David and withdrawal from his lord. Lowercase lord here refers to the human superior within Abijah's speech.

Retain pestilent/lawless followers, singular he opposing Rehoboam, younger and cowardly heart, and failure to withstand him. These are the speaker's characterizations, not corrections to the prior accession age.
column3: The comparative younger and the antecedent of the final him remain contextual questions; no precise age is inferred here.

column2: Retain the present claim to resist the Lord's kingdom through David's sons, the great multitude and golden calves made as gods. The accusatory comparison is kept as speech rather than narrator endorsement.

Retain expulsion of Aaronite priests and Levites, priests from the land's people, filled hands with one calf and seven rams, and priesthood to a god who does not exist. The selected singular god is not made plural.
column3: Fill hands is a consecration idiom, but the reading does not invent additional ritual actions or qualifications.

column2: Retain claimed non-abandonment, Aaron's sons ministering and Levites in their courses. The selected speech distinguishes these roles without adding a new priestly office.

Retain burnt offerings morning/evening, compound incense, bread on the pure table, lampstand and evening lamps, and the contrast of keeping and abandoning. Burn rather than merely incense accommodates the selected verb's application to whole offerings.

Retain the Lord in command, priests, signal trumpets and the affirmative future you will fight against the Lord, followed by lack of success. Do not insert a missing not to make a familiar prohibition.
column3: The pragmatic force of the affirmative future as warning or question merits review; the selected clause has no negative before fight.

column2: Retain Jeroboam sending the ambush behind and himself in front of Judah. The two-front arrangement is preserved rather than assigning both positions to the same contingent.
Retain Judah turning, explicit behold, battle in front and behind, cry to the Lord and priests' trumpets. The sequence describes recognition and response before the divine strike.
Retain the repeated Judahite cry and the Lord striking Jeroboam and Israel before Abijah and Judah. The explicit divine agent is not replaced with the shouting army.
Retain Israel fleeing and the Lord delivering them into Judah's hands. The two plural pronouns denote opposed groups, as established by the preceding names.
Retain the great blow and 500,000 mighty men falling wounded. Do not silently convert the casualty expression into a confirmed count of killed men or reduce the stated number.
Retain Israel humbled and Judah prevailing because of hope in the ancestral God. The contrasting outcomes and the stated reason remain.
Retain Baithel, Isana and Ephron with each city's villages. The repeated dependent settlements remain rather than being omitted from the captured territory.
Retain Jeroboam's lack of strength again throughout Abijah's days and the Lord striking him before death. No date or explanation is added to reconcile the regnal chronology.
Retain Abijah growing strong, fourteen wives, twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters. The family totals are not inferred from another king's household.
Retain remaining deeds, acts and words in Addo's prophetic book. Both deeds and words remain, without identifying the book as an extant modern title.
Retain died with his fathers, burial, Asa's succession and Judah's ten years of quiet under Asa. This entire sequence remains in chapter 13 rather than shifting its end into chapter 14.
Retain doing good and right before his God. The unnamed subject continues Asa from the selected preceding chapter's final unit.
Retain foreigners' altars, high places, shattered pillars and cut groves. No later high-place qualification is imported to remove an apparent tension.
Retain the command to Judah to seek the ancestral God and do both law and commandments. The two objects remain distinct.

Propose he was at peace for he made peace. The selected intransitive peace verb has no object and is repeated with the land as subject in verse 5; the proposal avoids suggesting an unexpressed act of peacemaking. Retain removal of altars and idols from all cities and the continuation semicolon; the close stage preserves the inherited wording.
Retain the initial walled-cities fragment, land at peace, no war in those years and the Lord's giving rest. Do not add a missing he built verb to resolve the selected fragment.
column3: The attachment of walled cities across the verse 4–5 boundary remains unresolved; the reading is deliberately provisional at this point.

column2: Retain building cities, walls, towers, gates and bars while holding the land, and reciprocal seeking: they sought God and He sought them. Rest and prospering are both divine actions; no repeated they sought Him replaces He sought us.
Retain 300,000 Judean shield/spear bearers and 250,000 Benjaminite light-shield bearers and archers. The figures and differentiated equipment are not harmonized with another military list.
Retain Zare the Ethiopian, a thousand thousands, 300 chariots and arrival at Marisa. The large number and its repeated-thousand form remain without a speculative scaling.
Retain Asa meeting him and the ravine north of Marisa. North is selected; no named valley from another witness replaces it.

Retain God's ability to save with many or few, strengthening request, trust, advance in His name and no human prevailing against Him. Thy/Thee mark direct prayer, and no unexpressed against is inserted between many and few.
Retain the Lord striking Ethiopians before Judah and the Ethiopians fleeing. The repeated ethnic designation makes the fleeing group explicit.
Retain pursuit to Gedor, no preservation among the fallen, shattering before the Lord and His force and much spoil. Do not replace Gedor with Gerar or claim a precise number of survivors.
column3: No preservation is an awkward provisional rendering; the scope of peripoiesis and the referent of His force require review.

column2: Retain villages around Gedor, terror from the Lord, all their cities plundered and abundant spoil. Villages and cities are both selected and not reduced to one settlement category.

Retain tents of possessions, the Amazonians, many sheep and camels and return to Jerusalem. Do not silently substitute livestock camps alone or identify the group with a conjectural historical population.
column3: Amazonians and its appositional relationship to the tents remain unresolved textual and lexical questions, not a claim of established historical identity.
